sections.name: Definition
sections.content: At its simplest, a data center is just a building that houses technology infrastructure such as servers, data storage systems, networking devices, and operating systems. Previously, companies would own a data center to facilitate their computing needs. Nowadays, cloud service providers (CSPs) own massive data centers capable of fulfilling the needs for multiple separate companies at once.
